                     </ns0:gap> or <ns0:hi>vessel.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> door <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bably by the chamber of the Princes is meant some chamber where the Princes were wont to meet in a Court, or for Coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sel. Thither <ns0:hi>Ieremiah</ns0:hi> brings these <ns0:hi>Rechabites,</ns0:hi> and sets vessels of Wine before them, not commanding them to drink it, but on<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly inviting them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 And I set before the sons of the house of the Rechabites pots full of wine, and cups, and I said unto them, Drink ye wine.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 But they said, We will drink no wine: for Jonadab the son of Rechab our father <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">It is uncertain whether <ns0:hi>father</ns0:hi> here signifies their immedi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ate Parent, or (which is more probable) their Progenitor; it is most likely it referreth to that <ns0:hi>Ionadab</ns0:hi> of whom we read 2 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 10.15. who was the father (that is the progenitor of this Family of the <ns0:hi>Rechabites,</ns0:hi> at 300 years distance.)</ns0:note> command<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed us, saying, Ye shall drink no wine, <ns0:hi>neither ye</ns0:hi> nor your sons for ever <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">The reason why he left his Posterity this charge is uncertain, proba<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bly to warn them against the Luxury which he saw began to abound in <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> and being desirous, that they should inure themselves to a more hardy and laborious life, being originally <ns0:hi>Kenites,</ns0:hi> and used to Husbandry, and keeping of sheep and other Cattel, he desired they should live according to their quality.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 Neither shall ye build house, nor sowe seed, nor plant vineyard, nor have <ns0:hi>any:</ns0:hi> but all your days ye shall dwell in tents, that ye may live many dayes in the land where ye <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> stran<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gers <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">The last words of the verse probably give us a reason of the former, they were no Native <ns0:hi>Jews,</ns0:hi> but strangers amongst them, who commonly are envied, when they are observed to thrive too much, or to live splendidly; and that envy of the Natives of the place where they sojourn, exposeth them to their Ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tred and Malice, so as their lives are made uneasie to them, <ns0:hi>Jonadab</ns0:hi> therefore cautions his Sons to avoid these inconvenien<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cies by a thrifty, sober, laborious life, to which they had been bred, in keeping Flocks, and to avoid any thing might expose them to Envy or Hatred or Malice of the People amongst whom they were come to sojourn.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 Thus have we obeyed the voice of Jona<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dab the son of Rechab our father, in all that he hath charged us, to drink no wine all our days, we, our wives, nor our sons, nor our daugh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ters.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 Nor to build houses for us to dwell in: nei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther have we vineyard, nor field, nor seed.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 But we have dwelt in tents <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Moveable Habitations, which they could with little labour remove from place to place, as they had convenience to feed their Flocks, this was their ordinary way of living until necessity compelled them to come and live in <ns0:hi>Jerusalem.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and have o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />beyed, and done according to all that Jonadab our father commanded us.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 But it came to pass when Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, came up into the land <ns0:note n="i." place="bottom">When the <ns0:hi>Chaldean</ns0:hi> Army came into the land, they saw there would be no quiet abode for them any where but in some fortified place. The <ns0:hi>Syrians</ns0:hi> joyned with the <ns0:hi>Chaldeans</ns0:hi> in this War, as we read 2 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 24.2. This they tell the Prophet was the reason why they who never used to dwell in Cities, nor fix<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed Houses, came to dwell at <ns0:hi>Jerusalem,</ns0:hi> to prevent being destroy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed by the forragers for these Armies.</ns0:note>, that we said, Come, and let us go to Jerusalem, for fear of the army of the Chaldeans, and for fear of the army of the Syrians; So we dwell at Jeru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />salem.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 ¶ Then came the word of the LORD unto Jeremiah, saying,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, Go, and tell the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, Will ye not receive in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />struction to hearken to my words? saith the LORD.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 The words of Jonadab the son of Rechab, that he commanded his sons not to drink wine,
<ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:47" />
are performed; for unto this day they drink none, but obey their fathers commandment: notwith<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />standing I have spoken unto you, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 7.13.25.</ns0:note> rising early, and speaking, but ye hearkned not unto me.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 I have sent also unto you all my servants the prophets, rising up early and sending <ns0:hi>them,</ns0:hi> saying, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 18.11. and 25.5.</ns0:note> Return ye now every man from his evil way, and amend your doings, and go not after other gods to serve them, and ye shall dwell in the land, which I have given to you, and to your fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers: but ye have not inclined your ear, nor hearkned to me <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">God in this Revelation of his Mind to the Prophet expound<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth to him, why he had set him to bring the <ns0:hi>Rechabites</ns0:hi> into the Temple, and commanded him to set Wine before them, and invite them to drink of it, that by their refusal of doing ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to the invitation, in obedience to their Father <ns0:hi>Iona<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dab</ns0:hi>; he might convince the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> of their disobedience to his commands, yet Gods commands were more advantaged, then the commands of <ns0:hi>Ionadab</ns0:hi> in that. 1. <ns0:hi>Ionadab</ns0:hi> was but an earth<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly Parent, and so had no absolute universal soveraignty over his children, but God was <ns0:hi>the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>Io<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nadabs</ns0:hi> command was not for the performance of a moral duty, but the doing of a thing which they might do, or leave undone. God required of them what was but their moral duty, and for which was the highest reason. 3. <ns0:hi>Ionadabs</ns0:hi> command had no promise annexed, Gods precept had a promise annexed, yet they had not yielded him that obedience which the sons of <ns0:hi>Ionadab</ns0:hi> had yielded him: He was their Father, but where was his honour.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 Because the sons of Jonadab the son of Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />chab have performed the commandement of their Father, which he commanded them, but this peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple hath not hearkned unto me;</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 Therefore thus saith the LORD God of hosts, the God of Israel, Behold, I will bring up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on Judah, and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lem, all the evil that I have pronounced against them: because I have spoken unto them, and they have not heard, I have called unto them, and they have not answered.<ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">This is but the same threatning confirmed, which we have often met with before, concerning the ruine of this people, only the meritorious cause of it is further amplified, their not paying that homage to God which these <ns0:hi>Rechabites</ns0:hi> paid to an Earthly parent, and had been steady in the payment of, now for three hundred years together.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 And Jeremiah said to the house of the Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />chabites, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, Because you have obeyed the command of Jonadab your father, and kept all his precepts, and done according to all that he hath commanded you.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 Therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts the God of Israel, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>There shall not a man be cut off from Ionadab the son of Rechab to stand,</ns0:hi> &c.</ns0:note> Jonadab the son of Rechab shall not want a man to stand before me for ever <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>For ever</ns0:hi> here signifies the <ns0:hi>ever</ns0:hi> of the Jewish State, or Church, whether the promise relates to the abiding of <ns0:hi>Ionadab</ns0:hi>'s <ns0:hi>Family,</ns0:hi> when many Families of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were quite rooted out, cut off, and extinct, or to some special favour that God would shew them, or to some place of Office, they should have in, or about the Temple (as some judge because 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 2.55. it appears they were <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi>) is uncertain: but it is a question of more moment. How God promiseth a reward to these sons of <ns0:hi>Iona<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dab</ns0:hi> for obeying the command of their Father, and whether they had sinned if they had not obeyed this command of <ns0:hi>Iona<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dab,</ns0:hi> which brings in another question: <ns0:hi>Whether Parents have a power to oblige their children in matters which God hath left at liberty.</ns0:hi> To which I answer, 1. <ns0:hi>God might reward these</ns0:hi> Rechabites, <ns0:hi>for their Reverence and Obedience to</ns0:hi> Jonadab <ns0:hi>their Father, though they were not strictly by the Divine Law, obliged thus far to have obeyed him</ns0:hi>: as he rewarded <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> for his thoughts in his heart to build him an house, though it was not God's will that he should do it, so as God's promise of the reward doth not prove their obedi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence in this particular to have been their Duty. Admit that it remained still a matter of Liberty, yet the General Honour, and Reverence they testified might be rewarded by God. 2. Unquestionably <ns0:hi>Parents have not a power to determine Children in all things as to which God hath left them a liberty,</ns0:hi> for then they have a power to make their children <ns0:hi>slaves,</ns0:hi> and to take away all their natural Liberty. To marry or not, and to this, or that person, is matter of <ns0:hi>Liberty.</ns0:hi> Parents cannot in this case deter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mine their Children, <ns0:hi>Beth<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>l Gen.</ns0:hi> 24.58. asketh <ns0:hi>Rebeccah if she wo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ld go with Abraham</ns0:hi>'s servant before he would send her. 3. <ns0:hi>In matters of civil concernment they have a far greater power than in matters of Religion,</ns0:hi> All Souls are God's, and Conscience can be under no other dominion than that of God. 4. <ns0:hi>In civil things Parents have a great power, d<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ring the nonage of Children, and af<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter, also in matters which concern their Parents good,</ns0:hi> as to command them to assist them, to help to supply their necessities, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> 5. <ns0:hi>Parents being set over Children, and instead of God to them as it is their Duty to advise their Children to the best of their ability for their good: so it is the Duty of children to receive their advice, and not to depart from it, unless they see circumstances so mistaken by Pa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rents, or so altered by the providence of God, as they may reasonably judge, their Parents, had they known or foreseen it, would not have so advised.</ns0:hi> But that Parents have an absolute power to deter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mine Children in all things as to which God hath not forbidden them, and that Children by the Law of God are obliged to an Obedience to all such Commands, however, they may see their Parents mistaken, or God by his Providence may have al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tered circumstances I see no reason to conclude. <ns0:hi>Ionadab</ns0:hi> had prudently advised his Sons as before mentioned, they were things they might do, and which by experience they found not hurtful to them, but of great profit and advantage, and that with reference to all the ends of mans life: Herein they yield Obedience, and pay a Reverence to their Parent, this pleaseth God, he promiseth to reward them with the continuance of their Family, according to what he had said, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 20.12. in the Fifth Commandment, which the Apostle calleth the First Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mandement with promise.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
